key_insight: When diagnoses include cases not detectable from model inputs, selective testing can make AI predictions appear accurate in tested patients yet reverse in untested patients.
clinical_relevance: ECG-based ACS models may not generalize beyond catheterized patients, making target selection and evaluation in the intended population essential.
method: Formalized target recoverability under selective diagnostic testing.
Simulated increasing testing selectivity and input-undetectable cases.
Fine-tuned three ECG foundation models on revascularization and compared subtype-specific targets.
evidence_signal: Revascularization-trained models achieved AUROC 0.740–0.770 among catheterized patients but 0.381–0.478 for 30-day major adverse cardiovascular events among untested patients; ECG-visible subtype models retained discrimination at 0.680–0.709.
watch_item: Revascularization was an ACS proxy, and untested-patient evaluation used a different outcome, complicating direct performance comparisons.
paper_title: Target Recoverability under Selective Labels: A Failure Mode in ECG-Based Acute Coronary Syndrome Prediction
